confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from six web searches, which returned search summaries only. I did not open the underlying pages. The sources are crowd-sourced or aggregated price indexes (Numbeo via Expatica, Expatistan, MyLifeElsewhere, CityCost, and travel guides). They mostly quote AUD, and I converted to USD using the RBA rate. Beer, cappuccino and the inexpensive meal are fairly consistent across sources: draft beer about AUD 12-13, cappuccino about AUD 5.5-6, inexpensive meal about AUD 25.5. The mid-range meal for two (about AUD 100-120) is less certain because sources disagree. Cocktail is based on a downtown-club figure of about AUD 22 and a travel-guide range of AUD 18-28. The wine glass is based on a travel-guide range of about AUD 12-16 for house wine, which is consistent with typical beer-to-wine ratios. Cocktail and wine are the weakest food and drink anchors. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Melbourne for a July (winter, lower-demand) pricing window. I did not search for accommodation prices or inspect any booking pages or listings. The RBA rate is the latest observation found (18 November 2026), which is later than the July 2026 pricing window.
comparable_city_reasoning: No comparable city used. Melbourne is priced directly from Melbourne-specific sources, with Sydney and other Australian capitals as a general sanity check for accommodation.
